problem: "Page caches and routing tables use hash tables" is wrong for the Linux kernel that the rest of the paragraph assumes. Linux keeps page-cache pages in a radix tree (now the XArray), not a hash table, and routing entries in a trie (LC-trie / FIB trie), not a hash table. A student who repeats this in an exam or viva is repeating an inaccurate claim.
fix: "Kernel hash tables include the dentry (directory entry) cache, the inode cache and connection-tracking tables; the Linux page cache uses a radix tree (XArray) and routing entries use a trie."

problem: "A tree stores parent-child order" is vague; a reader may not see what is actually stored.
fix: "A tree stores items in a hierarchy: each node has one parent and zero or more children."

problem: The sentence "a VM runs its own guest kernel; a container shares the host kernel" appears three times (Section 2 body, last line of Section 2, and trap 3) in a short chapter.
fix: Keep the full contrast in the Section 2 body only; in the trap list shorten to "Container = shared host kernel, no guest kernel."
